project: AWS Cloud Security Misconfiguration Assessment & Remediation

findings.title: Over-Permissioned IAM Identity
findings.initial_state: An IAM user policy granted s3:* against Resource *.
findings.risk: The identity could perform unnecessary and destructive S3 actions beyond its intended read-only requirement.
findings.remediation: Replaced wildcard S3 privileges with s3:ListBucket and s3:GetObject scoped to one lab bucket.
findings.validation: IAM Access Analyzer check-access-not-granted changed from FAIL to PASS for s3:DeleteBucket, s3:PutBucketPolicy, and s3:DeleteObject.

findings.title: Proposed Public S3 Resource Policy
findings.initial_state: A simulated S3 resource policy used Principal * with s3:GetObject.
findings.risk: If deployed, the policy could expose bucket objects to public access.
findings.remediation: Replaced the wildcard principal with one explicit IAM identity and retained S3 Block Public Access protections.
findings.validation: IAM Access Analyzer check-no-public-access changed from FAIL to PASS.

findings.title: S3 Versioning Disabled
findings.initial_state: The lab bucket did not have object versioning enabled.
findings.risk: Object overwrites or deletions would have reduced recovery options.
findings.validation: AWS CLI returned Enabled and the post-remediation Prowler scan no longer reported s3_bucket_object_versioning as failed.

limitations: The intentionally public S3 bucket policy was evaluated but never deployed.
Prowler evaluated broader IAM and S3 account posture beyond the deliberately created lab findings.
The IAM remediation was validated directly with IAM Access Analyzer; the aggregate Prowler IAM failure count did not change.
Raw Prowler reports are excluded from the public repository because they contain account-specific metadata.
